thread:
amal: security-bot flagged a potential AWS access key in last night's CI artifacts for repo payments-service. saw an AKIA... token in the CircleCI log :rotating_light:
security-bot: automated alert: gitleaks v8 detected high-confidence secret in artifact path /tmp/circleci-artifacts/payments/2026-02-28/log.txt commit abc123 (rule: AWS Access Key). report: https://internal/reports/gitleaks/1749256789.json
leo: omg. which key exactly? do we know if it was used?
emily: steps: 1) revoke the key 2) rotate creds in vault 3) audit CI logs/org repos for similar leaks 4) remove secret from git history 5) communicate to stakeholders.
jonah: I'm revoking now. running: aws iam update-access-key --access-key-id AKIAEXAMPLE123 --status Inactive (will post confirmation)
jonah: revoked the key, creating replacement in vault and updating infra secrets. redeploying consumers that reference it. (reacted with :white_check_mark:)
amal: thanks. jonah please paste the new key id (not the secret) and update ticket INFRA-2345 so we can track rotation. also need to confirm whether the leaked key was used by checking CloudTrail and S3 access logs.
leo: i'll query CloudTrail for the last 72h for that access-key-id and list S3/STS calls. will report back.
amal: also we need to scrub the git history. payments-service has some large binary blobs, so prefer git-filter-repo. proposed commands:

```
# mirror clone
git clone --mirror git@github.com:redwood/payments-service.git
# remove commits/files containing the secret pattern
git filter-repo --replace-refs delete-no-add --path-rename : --invert-paths --pattern 'AKIA[A-Z0-9]+'
# push force
git push --force --all
```

leo: be careful pushing --force for an active repo. we'll coordinate a short maintenance window with the team. also raise a PR to bump dependent submodule refs if any.
security-bot: queued org-wide scan: running gitleaks with regex for AWS keys and other provider tokens across 220 repos. set to save findings to /internal/sec/reports/ci-leak-1749256789.json
emily: we should also scan CI build logs (CircleCI/GHA) for tokens — some tokens are only in artifacts. quick grep command for infra to run across archived logs:

```
grep -R --exclude-dir=artifacts 'AKIA' /var/ci-archives/* || true
```

infra-team: starting log grep across archived CI runs. we'll also check third-party artifact storage buckets for public exposure.
jonah: to avoid future leakage, enabling repository-level pre-push hooks and server-side gitleaks in the GitHub org. rolling out a deploy to block pushes with high-confidence matches.
amal: also need to mask environment variables in CI logs. for GitHub Actions use environment secrets (not exported) and add 

```
- name: Mask secret
  run: echo "::add-mask::$MY_SECRET"
```

and in CircleCI use built-in env var masking and set `no_output_timeout` accordingly.
legal: please @amal add a short incident summary for legal review. confirm whether any customer data was accessed with the leaked key. if not, lower severity, but we still need a retention/notification assessment.
amal: noted. i'll draft a one-pager and link CloudTrail/scan evidence.
leo: CloudTrail shows a handful of STS:GetCallerIdentity calls from an IP we don't recognize around the time of the leak; digging into whether it maps to CI runner IP ranges.
platform-sre: if the key was used outside expected CI ranges, rotate any credentials that shared same IAM policy (role-equivalent). also enable session restrictions and require STS role-assumption via short-lived credentials where possible.
emily: post-incident actions for backlog: 1) enable org-level server-side gitleaks 2) add pre-commit hook with secrets detection 3) require KMS-backed secrets in Vault for long-lived credentials and forbid embedding plaintext creds in repos/CI 4) add build-log scrubbing for all pipelines 5) run a retro audit of build logs for the last 180 days
amal: assigning owners: infra-team for history scrub + force push coordination, security-bot/task for org-scan and enforcement, legal for notification assessment, platform-sre for short-lived creds plan. will create an incident ticket and postmortem template.
jonah: scrub completed locally, will coordinate force-push at 0300 UTC. pushed new vault tokens and redeployed consumers. smoke tests passing.
leo: CloudTrail follow-up: we traced activity to a known CircleCI runner IP range and no suspicious S3 writes were made, only a few ReadApis from internal build buckets. marking potential external access as low.
amal: thanks all. next steps: complete postmortem, add automated CI log scanning, and schedule org runbook update for secrets in CI. closing thread once postmortem link is up. :lock:
